anchor.section: A. Shell commands and scheme paths
C1. `bash` refuses any command that mentions a registered scheme (critical, live)

quote.exact: - **G8.20 Scheme commands.** A standalone `ls`, `cat`, `rm`, `mv`, `cp` or `mkdir` (or a `>` redirect) whose path arguments use a registered non-locatable scheme (e.g. `rm secret://global/old-token`) runs in-process through the resource router with that provider's approval rules, and returns shell-like output and exit status. Any other command with such a path fails with an error naming the supported forms. Scheme paths in commands for an `ssh://` cwd fail explicitly.
